archetype.name: Point Guard (short-area distributor)
archetype.definition: This year Mahomes is a quick-game distributor. He works off a 5.7-yard intended air depth, spreads the ball behind the line and underneath, and lets Travis Kelce and the intermediate middle do most of the damage.

report.headline: Mahomes has turned distributor: efficient underneath, clean pocket, no deep game.
report.take:
The 2026 version of Mahomes is not the one his early career would suggest. His intended air yards sit at 5.7 and his aggressiveness rate is 6.84, the lowest tight-window rate on his record and 6.5 points below last season's 13.3. He has thrown 74 passes behind the line and 126 more inside 10 yards, against just 25 at 20-plus. The offense has been rebuilt around timing and completion. His completion rate jumped 4.6 points from a 2025 season in which he ranked 40th, and his CPOE has climbed from 0.3 to 2.14. The result is a solid quarterback rather than a dominant one: 0.149 EPA per dropback ranks 16th of 49, comfortably above a league average near zero, on a 6-2 team.

Two things drive the efficiency. The first is the intermediate zone. On 38 throws between 10 and 19 yards he is producing 0.688 EPA per attempt with a 7.9 CPOE, and that is where Kelce lives. Kelce's 48 targets have returned 25.8 EPA, the bulk of everything the passing game has produced. The second is the under-center game. Those 72 plays run at 0.254 EPA with a 59.7% success rate, against 0.111 out of shotgun, which points to play-action and the league's second-best rushing offense setting up his throws. The quick release has also fixed his sack problem. A 17% pressure-to-sack rate ranks 4th, after 0.273 and 0.288 the previous two years, and it is back in line with his 2019-2022 range.

The numbers also hide some costs. The deep ball has collapsed: 7 of 25 completed, -10.8 CPOE, two interceptions, negative EPA. That is a 25-throw sample, and the same is true of his deep game every year, but it fits a quarterback and a scheme that have stopped asking for it. Xavier Worthy, the nominal vertical threat, has drawn 47 targets for 0.01 EPA per target, essentially dead volume. The legs are fading from the offense as well. He is running for 10.6 yards a game, down 19.5 from last year, with only two designed runs, though his 15 scrambles still pay at 0.308 EPA each.

The recent trend is softer. Over the last five games his EPA per dropback is 0.051 below his season mark and his TD rate 1.1 points lower. The Seattle game drags that down: a -6.0 EPA dud against the league's fifth-best defense. Denver and the Jets games since then were solid. Now an elbow strain makes him questionable, and his final game before it, against the Jets, featured a season-low 2.8 intended air yards. If the elbow lingers, this offense is built to absorb it, because it already lives short. It just cannot afford to lose more of the downfield game it barely has.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle with Kelce
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 yards are his best area by a distance, with high EPA and a large positive CPOE. Kelce is the engine, turning 48 targets into 25.8 EPA. The throws suit Mahomes' timing and anticipation, and the TE connection has held up all year, so it should last, but it is concentrated in one player.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance is back
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate has dropped to 17%, 4th among qualifiers, from 28.8% last year. That comes from a quicker, shorter process: a 2.72-second time to throw, with lots of answers behind the line. Because it is a schematic choice, it should hold for as long as the offense stays this short.

strengths.title: Red-zone precision
strengths.body: He has 12 touchdowns on 44 red-zone attempts, with a 15.1 CPOE. Most of his scoring comes from tight-area accuracy on short throws near the goal line. The TD rate is the part most likely to cool on this volume, but the accuracy behind it is real.

concerns.title: The deep ball has disappeared
concerns.body: He has completed 28% of his 20-plus-yard throws, with a -10.8 CPOE and two interceptions, for negative EPA. It is a small sample, but it pairs with a career-low aggressiveness rate and Worthy's near-zero EPA per target, so this looks like a real gap in the offense rather than bad luck. It caps the ceiling against defenses that squeeze the underneath game.

concerns.title: Elbow strain on a throwing arm
concerns.body: He is questionable and day-to-day with an elbow strain. His final game before it was his shortest-throwing game of the year. A quarterback already avoiding the deep ball could lean even shorter, which squeezes the yardage ceiling more than the efficiency.

concerns.title: Rushing value has dried up
concerns.body: He is running for 10.6 yards a game, down 19.5 from last season's career-high form, with only two designed runs. Scrambles still produce, but the offense has pulled him out of the run game. That takes away a floor-raiser in both real and fantasy terms.

trend.note: He opened hot against Indianapolis and Miami, then dipped through a five-game stretch that included a -6.0 EPA loss at Seattle. Denver and the Jets were solid rebounds, but his last-five EPA per dropback still trails his season mark.

nextGame.headline: Middling Falcons defense; the elbow is the real variable
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense is average almost everywhere against the pass: 15th in pass EPA allowed, and 15th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks. Its strengths are a 6th-ranked QB hit rate and good deep defense, ranked 7th in deep EPA. Neither troubles a Mahomes who rarely throws deep, but the hits matter more with a sore elbow. Its weaknesses line up with Kansas City's offense: the defense ranks 20th in rush EPA and 30th in explosive runs allowed, and backs see an above-league share of targets against it. Atlanta's offense ranks 28th in pass EPA, so the Chiefs are 3.5-point favorites and likely to play from ahead, where Mahomes has been efficient but throws less.

Availability drives this one. Mahomes himself is questionable with the elbow, and he was described as day-to-day. Left tackle Jaylon Moore, an 87%-snap starter, is questionable with an ankle; losing him would test the quick-game protection against a team that hits the quarterback. Worthy is questionable with a hamstring, but given how little his targets have produced, his absence could push more volume to Rashee Rice and Noah Gray at little cost. On Atlanta's side, edge rusher Samson Ebukam is on IR, which removes a part-time pass rusher. The forecast is mild under a retractable roof.

keyMatchups.title: Second receivers against a soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta has allowed 0.53 EPA per target to opposing WR2s, 29th in the league. In Kansas City's distribution that means Rice, especially if Worthy sits. It is a small-sample rank, but it fits Mahomes' spread-it-around approach.

keyMatchups.title: Kelce against a stingy TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta holds tight ends slightly under their averages and allows only 0.04 EPA per TE1 target, 10th best. Kelce carries the passing game, so if he is muted Mahomes has to find value elsewhere. That is the main risk to an efficient day.

keyMatchups.title: Hits on a sore elbow
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gets to the quarterback often, with the 6th-ranked hit rate, though it ranks only 18th in sack rate. Mahomes' quick game avoids sacks, but with Moore's status uncertain, the hits he does take matter more than usual.

nextGame.watch: How far downfield he throws early. If the elbow keeps his intended air yards near the Week 9 level, expect an efficient, low-ceiling day built on Kelce, the backs and the run game.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation holds up. The quick game, the sack avoidance, the under-center efficiency and the Kelce connection are schematic, and they have held across all eight games. That makes 0.12-0.16 EPA per dropback a fair expectation, with passing yards in the 230-270 range most weeks and two-TD games when the red zone cooperates. Two things should regress: the red-zone TD rate is running hot and will likely cool toward 1.4-1.9 TDs a game, and the deep ball should improve somewhat from a 28% completion rate simply through sample growth.

The ceiling depends on whether Kansas City restores a vertical element. Worthy's targets have been empty, and the elbow argues against more deep shots soon. Kansas City passes more than situations predict, which protects his volume, but the league's second-best rushing offense and a good defense mean plenty of games where he manages a lead rather than chasing. Expect a top-12-to-16 quarterback with a sturdier weekly floor than last year and fewer big games.
swingFactors: Elbow recovery and its effect on throw depth
Whether a vertical threat emerges beyond Worthy

confidence.note: Eight games of a consistent, schematic profile, but an elbow strain and a small deep-ball sample add uncertainty.
